steps.question: Half of this butterfly is missing. Which picture completes it?

options.whyWrong: B slides the same wing over without flipping it. That's a translation, not a reflection.
C turns the wing upside down (a 180° rotation). A mirror flips left and right only.
D has the right shape, but its spots don't match the other side.

steps.hint: Imagine folding the page along the body. Both halves should land on each other exactly.

polya.understand: The missing half must match the half you can see, as if the page were folded along the body.
polya.plan: Picture each option folded onto the left wing. Which one lands exactly, spots and all?
polya.lookBack: Check one spot: the big dark spot must be the same distance from the body on both sides.

steps.explanation: A butterfly has reflection symmetry: the body is a line of symmetry, and each wing is the mirror image of the other. Every point on the left has a matching point the same distance away on the right.
steps.why: Left–right symmetry is common in animals that move in one direction, like butterflies, fish, and people.

steps.question: This snowflake lost an arm. The arms are spaced evenly. How many degrees apart are they?

options.whyWrong: 72° = 360° ÷ 5. That counts only the five arms you can see, not the missing one.
90° = 360° ÷ 4 would give a snowflake with four arms.

steps.hint: A full turn is 360°. How many arms would a complete snowflake have?

polya.understand: The arms are evenly spaced around one full turn of 360°.
polya.plan: Count the arms a complete snowflake would have, including the missing one, then share 360° between them.
polya.lookBack: 6 × 60° = 360°, so six turns of 60° bring the snowflake all the way around.

steps.explanation: A complete snowflake has 6 arms, so the arms are 360° ÷ 6 = 60° apart. Turning it by 60° lands it on itself: six-fold rotational symmetry. Ice crystals grow this way because water molecules lock into a hexagonal pattern.
steps.why: Snowflakes get their six-fold shape from the hexagonal way water molecules freeze.
